row.body: The keyring is clipped to a blank page in the studio desk. The only pencilled line says “doors locked”; the box for who checked them is empty.
row.title: The studio key clipped to a blank rundown

sidecar.gloss: A locked studio and an unsigned check remain on the same page.
sidecar.rival_reading: A broadcast worker could secure the studio before any emergency and leave the checklist unfinished; the blank box does not prove a failed containment order.

row.body: three pickup dots mark the open wrench and hand radio. two were scratched away without wear around them.
row.title: missing count beside the open wrench

sidecar.gloss: A response bundle preserves a missing count, changed route, or erased identity.
sidecar.rival_reading: A farm-program crew could have counted routes, repacked tools, or removed ownership marks during hurried field work; the objects do not prove a concealed public response.

row.body: The notebook is trapped beneath a glass desk cover. A crop-row sketch has a water stain across its center; the bottle beside it is dry and capped.
row.title: The field sketch under the studio glass

sidecar.gloss: A field sketch and a water mark sit under the studio desk glass.
sidecar.rival_reading: A reporter could sketch field reports and spill water while working; neither the stain nor the drawing identifies a program.
